mechanism: Resolution Fallback {{strategy}}. When a Pattern_ID is not found in local storage, the system attempts to resolve it via secondary channels (Inline Payload -> Network Request) rather than halting immediately. Crucially, any definition acquired this way must be cryptographically verified against the requested Pattern_ID. It defaults to {{fail_closed}} if verification fails, but attempts to parse verified inline definitions to maintain continuity.
gloss: When verification fails, fall back to inline definition
failure_modes: Hash Mismatch: Inline definition claims to be Pattern#X but hashes to Pattern#Y (Spoofing).
DoS via Definition: Sender includes massive multi-megabyte 'definition' to exhaust receiver memory.
Dependency Hell: Inline definition references other unknown patterns, triggering recursive lookups.
invariants: A definition enters local storage only if it validates fully.
An externally acquired definition is hashed and verified against the requested ID before loading.
Expands inline definitions no deeper than `max_recursion_depth`.
preconditions: {{message}} contains fallback data OR sender is reachable
postconditions: Pattern resolved and locally minted OR Transaction aborted

parameters.name: max_def_size
parameters.description: Largest inline definition accepted, in bytes. Deliberately uncapped; default 100KB.

parameters.name: max_recursion_depth
parameters.description: Depth of inline-definition expansion permitted before the chain is refused.
